correctness_confidence.basis: Checked independently: the sec. 6 witness for C5[K9] reproduces exactly (K positive, inertia (1,1,5); 5x5 auxiliary Hessian inertia (2,3,0); pin -255/256 gives (1,4,0)). Counts (5) and (6) match brute force for (s,k) in {(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(2,4)}. The odd-cycle claims for s>=20 and the sec. 5 tables rest on certificate files absent from the PDF, so they are unverified.

rigor.basis: Lemmas 3 and 4 are coherent on inspection, but Prop. 5 and the bounded-size tables depend on exact coefficient certificates, and the symbolic matrix T (eqs. 8-11) is only described verbally. The infinite-family claim cannot be checked from the submission. The even-m case depends on the six-spin theorem of [5].

novelty.basis: The uniform odd-cycle construction, outside the independence-stable theorem of [5], is a new target relative to the clique result [2]. The minimum-edge occupation classification (Lemma 4) is specific to this family. Novelty depends on [2], [3], [4] and [5], which I could not check; no priority search was done.

significance.basis: Settles Lorentzianity for one two-parameter family (uniform cycle clique blowups) and gives a characterization within it (Corollary 2). It does not give a general connected-source result, an optimal state bound or a fixed target. Scope is narrow but relevant to the converse question in [3].

reproducibility.basis: The supplementary JSON certificates, the symbolic matrix and the executable verifier are cited but not supplied in the submitted folder. Only the sec. 6 witness is fully stated, and it was reproduced exactly. The remaining claims cannot be re-derived from the manuscript.

summary: Hostile but fair review of the exact PDF (SHA-256 verified). The explicit finite witness for C5[K9] in sec. 6 reproduces: the 5x5 auxiliary Hessian has inertia (2,3,0), and the minimum-edge counts (5) and (6) match brute force in four small cases. However, the general odd-cycle theorem (all s>=2, q<=10) rests on exact certificates and a symbolic matrix that are not in the submission and could not be verified. The even-m case depends on unverified prior work [5]. Recommendation: major revision.
strengths: The sec. 6 witness for C5[K9] is explicit and reproduces: K = 11^T - aa^T has positive entries and inertia (1,1,5), and the auxiliary 5x5 Hessian has inertia (2,3,0).
Lemma 4 (minimum-edge occupations on odd cycles) and count (6) are correct on every tested case.
The scope is stated honestly: no optimality, no general connected-source characterization and no priority claim. Failed trials are reported; the pin -255/256 gives (1,4,0).

The reduction in eqs. (2)-(4) and Lemma 3 is internally consistent on inspection: the Hessian dimensions match, the factor (1-theta)^e0 is positive, and the identity (UD)_ir = l a_i (1-l a_i)^r holds.
weaknesses: Prop. 5 and the sec. 5 tables are asserted from certificate files (odd-initial-five-symbolic.json, odd-initial-small-certificates.json) that are not part of the submission.
Eqs. (8)-(11) define the symbolic matrix T only verbally, so T for s>=20 cannot be reconstructed from the PDF.
The even-m six-state claim depends on the six-spin theorem of [5], an external working paper not included in the submission.
The limit argument in Lemma 3 (delta down to 0, then ell to -1) is sketched. The claim that inactive and higher-edge contributions vanish is asserted, not bounded.
potential_errors: Sec. 5, s = 4: the exceptions are k = 3..7, and the text gives a six-profile block only for k = 3, 4, 5. The block for k = 6, 7 is not identified, although the table lists a largest finite size of 6.
Sec. 3: the remark that each nontrivial clique class contains maximum-degree true twins is not explained and does not obviously bear on the argument.
strong_novelty_candidates: A uniform construction for odd cycles C_(2k+1)[K_s] with at most ten states, obtained from the minimum-edge occupation classification (Lemma 4) and an initial-profile compression (Lemma 3). Subject to a literature check that I did not perform.
unresolved_material_objections: Theorem 1 for odd m and all s>=2 (including q<=10 and q<=7 for s>=9) rests on Prop. 5 and the sec. 5 certificates. Their data files and the verifier are absent from the submitted PDF, and the symbolic matrix T is not written out. The claimed inertia cannot be checked from the manuscript. If any certificate fails, the general odd-cycle claim fails.

The even-m six-state claim relies on the six-spin theorem of [5], an external working paper that is not part of the submission and could not be checked here. If that result fails, the even-m part of Theorem 1 is unsupported.
